ideal-weight-calculator.formula:
Devine (1974): male 50 + 2.3 x (inches over 5 ft); female 45.5 + 2.3 x (inches over 5 ft).
Robinson (1983): male 52 + 1.9 x (inches over 5 ft); female 49 + 1.7 x (inches over 5 ft).
Miller (1983): male 56.2 + 1.41 x (inches over 5 ft); female 53.1 + 1.36 x (inches over 5 ft).
All results in kg.
howTo: Pick metric (cm) or imperial (ft/in) and enter your height.
Read your healthy weight from three classic formulas: Devine, Robinson and Miller.
Use the range they agree on as your reference band.
Compare with your BMI healthy range for a second opinion.
keyFacts: Ideal body weight (IBW) formulas date back to Devine's 1974 paper for drug dosing.
All three formulas add weight per inch above 5 feet (60 inches).
Women's formulas start about 4-5 kg lower than men's at the same height.
A 5'9" man gets 70.7 kg (Devine), 69.1 kg (Robinson) and 68.9 kg (Miller).
The formulas usually sit inside the BMI healthy range of 18.5-24.9.
They describe a reference, not a prescription: frame and muscle shift real targets.
